description: Golden cases for separation (final) pay: pro-rated 13th month, unused-leave monetization, the PHP 90,000 exemption pool, year-end tax true-up on the final payout, and the order in which a short payout is applied to tax, statutory and loan deductions. Regular payroll runs do not compute 13th month, so this is the path that does. Every expected value is hand-derived below from the published rules, never copied from engine output.

sources.thirteenth: PD 851 and its Revised Guidelines: 13th month pay is 1/12 of the basic salary earned within the calendar year; a separated employee is paid the pro-rated amount, less any 13th month already paid.
sources.exemption: TRAIN (RA 10963) Sec. 32(B)(7)(e): 13th month pay and other benefits are exempt up to 90,000 combined; the excess is taxable compensation. Leave monetization and separation pay are not part of that pool in the engine and are taxable unless the case states a taxable amount of zero.
sources.bir: Annual graduated rates effective 2023 onward: up to 250,000 exempt; 250,000-400,000 at 15% of the excess over 250,000; 400,000-800,000 at 22,500 + 20% over 400,000; 800,000-2,000,000 at 102,500 + 25% over 800,000; 2,000,000-8,000,000 at 402,500 + 30% over 2,000,000. Taxable = gross compensation - exempt benefit pool - employee statutory contributions.
sources.finalPay: DOLE Labor Advisory 06-20: final pay is released within 30 days from separation unless a company policy or agreement provides otherwise.

assumptions: The default (flag off) peso arithmetic is certified; the exact-centavo 13th month flag is a separate release control and none of the amounts below sit on a half-centavo.
All employees are non-MWE unless the case says so, with no de minimis and no other benefits.
Tax collected or refunded is the annualized tax due minus tax already withheld year to date. A collection is taken first from the final payout, then statutory deductions, then loans.
Gross compensation year to date is basic pay only (without the 13th month, which the final-pay computation adds itself).

yearEndSeparationCollectsTax.description: Resigns on December 31 with 11 months released (550,000) + 50,000 unpaid = 600,000 basic; 13th month 50,000. Annual gross 550,000 + 50,000 + 50,000 = 650,000; exempt pool 50,000; statutory 11,000; taxable 589,000. Tax = 22,500 + 20% x (589,000 - 400,000) = 22,500 + 37,800 = 60,300. Withheld 20,000, so 40,300 is collected. Gross final pay 100,000; net 100,000 - 40,300 = 59,700.

yearEndSeparationRefundsTax.description: Same earnings as the collection case but 80,000 was withheld during the year against 60,300 due: 19,700 is refunded and added to the payout. Available 100,000 + 19,700 = 119,700; no collection, no deductions: net 119,700.

thirteenthAlreadyPartlyPaid.description: Same 600,000 basic (13th month entitlement 50,000) but 25,000 was already paid as a mid-year advance: only 25,000 is due now. Annual gross 550,000 + 50,000 + 25,000 paid + 25,000 due = 650,000 - the same taxable 589,000 and tax 60,300; withheld 20,000 so 40,300 is collected. Gross final pay 50,000 + 25,000 = 75,000; net 75,000 - 40,300 = 34,700.

taxCollectionExceedsPayout.description: 13th month already fully paid (50,000) and only 2,000 of salary is unpaid: gross final pay 2,000. Annual gross 598,000 + 2,000 + 50,000 = 650,000; taxable 589,000; tax 60,300; nothing withheld, so 60,300 is owed. Only 2,000 can be applied; 58,300 is reported as unpaid tax and the net is 0. The shortfall must be surfaced, never silently dropped.

loanCappedByRemainingPay.description: The yearEndSeparationCollectsTax payout (after the 40,300 collection, 59,700 remains) with a 70,000 loan balance requested: only 59,700 can be deducted, 10,300 is deferred, and net is 0.

separationPayExemptWhenTaxableAmountIsZe.description: The collection case plus 200,000 separation pay that is exempt (involuntary cause, taxable amount 0). Tax is unchanged at 60,300, so collection stays 40,300. Gross final pay 100,000 + 200,000 = 300,000; net 300,000 - 40,300 = 259,700.

separationPayTaxableWhenNoExemptionState.description: Same 200,000 separation pay but no taxable amount stated, so the whole amount is treated as taxable compensation. Annual gross 650,000 + 200,000 = 850,000; taxable 850,000 - 50,000 - 11,000 = 789,000. Tax = 22,500 + 20% x 389,000 = 22,500 + 77,800 = 100,300. Withheld 20,000: 80,300 collected. Gross final pay 300,000; net 219,700.

minimumWageEarnerRefundsWithholding.description: MWE: basic 250,000 released + 50,000 unpaid = 300,000; 13th month 25,000 (inside the 90,000 pool, so exempt). Leave 10,000 is taxable supplementary compensation: taxable income = 10,000 - 0 statutory = 10,000, below 250,000: tax 0. 500 was wrongly withheld during the year and is refunded. Gross final pay = unpaid salary 50,000 + 13th month 25,000 + leave 10,000 = 85,000; net 85,000 + 500 refund = 85,500.

dueDates.description: 30 calendar days after a November 30 last day
leap day is counted in a leap year

limitations: Pure function certification of computeFinalPay: it does not exercise the Separation API route, approval workflow or payslip rendering.
Sub-centavo 13th month rounding belongs to the exact-centavo release flag and is not certified here.
The SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG year-to-date amounts are supplied as inputs; their derivation is certified in Phases 1 to 6.
Whether leave monetization and separation pay are taxable in a given case is a practitioner decision this suite takes as input.
